description.shortText: A low-temperature brain or full-body preservation technique aiming to prevent molecular structures from degrading after clinical death of the patient by maintaining the stability of tissues.

attachments.name: Cryonics: does it offer humanity a chance to return from the dead?
attachments.description: While it used to be the stuff of science fiction, the technology behind the dream has advanced in recent years

attachments.name: Putting dead heads on ice until the technology catches up
attachments.description: Tomorrow Biostasis charges €30–€100 per month to freeze heads or bodies. If the technology permits, they could well be resurrected.

attachments.name: China Cryonics Tech Can Freeze Human Body, Prevent Aging Till It Gets Proper Treatment
attachments.description: The cryonics institute is teaming up with the University of Science and Technology of China in Anhui province to research on preservation of pancreatic cells, as well as with Shandong University’s Qilu Hospital on the preservation of ovarian cells.

attachments.name: China explores cryopreservation with leading technologies but doubts remain about widespread adoption of technology
attachments.description: Gui Junmin has a dream to keep living on, so that someday in the future, he and his beloved wife Zhan Wenlian could meet again. On May 8, 2017, Zhan was announced clinically dead due to lung cancer in a hospital in Jinan, capital city of East China's Shandong Province.

attachments.name: Southern Cryonics: Australia’s first body-freezing facility attracting huge numbers
attachments.description: Do you want to be frozen after death in the hope that one day you could come back to life? Now you have your chance. 27 founding members have each contributed $50,000 to build the Southern Cryonics warehouse, which can house up to 40 bodies at a time for 500 years into the future.

attachments.name: A comparison between a new vitrification protocol and the slow freezing method in the cryopreservation of prepubertal testicular tissue
attachments.description: This study aimed to compare a new vitrification protocol with reduced cryoprotectant exposure to the slow freezing method in the cryopreservation of prepubertal rat testicular tissue.

attachments.name: The prospect of Immortality
attachments.description: Robert Ettinger founded the cryonics movement and authored The Prospect of Immortality, the first book about the idea of cryopreservation of humans.

attachments.name: Low temperature medicine
attachments.description: Cryogenic medicine is a new interdiscipline that has gradually formed with the development of life sciences, medicine, and cryogenic technology in recent decades. It is the most rapidly developed discipline in the field of life sciences and it is a emerging medical technologies that used cryogenic technology to treat human cells, tissues, and organs even the entire body to conduct cryogenic freezing, resuscitation, repair and treatment.
